name: MySQL
model: Tables of rows queried with SQL; JSON column type; vector type added in 9.0
engine_note: InnoDB: rows stored inside the primary-key B+tree (clustered index), secondary B-tree indexes, MVCC via undo logs, redo log
consistency: Multi-row transactions (InnoDB). Default repeatable read (snapshot for plain reads, but Jepsen shows it is weaker than the name); serializable optional. Redo log flushed on every commit by default. Replication async by default (semi-sync optional), so replica reads can be stale.

jepsen.version: 8.0.34 (also binlog replication and AWS RDS MySQL)
jepsen.finding: Repeatable read allows lost updates and other anomalies the SQL standard forbids, and RDS MySQL clusters routinely broke serializability; all six issues unresolved at publication.

scaling: Bigger machine; read replicas via binlog replication; Group Replication / InnoDB Cluster for failover; sharding is manual or via Vitess.
licence: GPLv2 (with linking exceptions); commercial licence and Enterprise Edition from Oracle
managed: Amazon RDS for MySQL / Aurora MySQL
version_note: 26.7 is an Innovation release and the first with calendar versioning (YY.M.P), after the 9.7 LTS series. The latest LTS is 9.7.3 (2026-08-18); 9.7.0 LTS shipped 2026-04-21.
reach: Reach for it when your team or framework already runs MySQL, for read-heavy web apps, or when you plan to shard with Vitess or PlanetScale.
avoid: Avoid when you rely on repeatable read to stop lost updates (use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or serializable), or need Postgres extensions.
escape: Not an escape so much as a peer; you pick it for an existing MySQL stack or the Vitess sharding path.
chat: Same as Postgres: users, chats and messages, if your stack is MySQL.
notes: Surprise: MySQL switched to calendar versioning; 26.7.0 (2026-07-28) is the first such release, an Innovation release, following 9.7 LTS. LICENSE file read from the trunk branch on 2026-10-04 (MySQL 26.7.0 Community, GPLv2 plus linking permissions). Defaults (REPEATABLE READ, innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=1, async replication) are standard MySQL defaults per the cited refman pages; not re-read page by page for 9.7.
